meta.title: Education & human capability
meta.updateStatus: World Bank / UNESCO UIS series refreshed; edition-pinned assessments and studies unchanged

question: Are people gaining the capabilities needed to adapt?

verdict.text: Foundational outcomes weakened in many measured systems and gaps persist. Vocational and adult-learning pathways expand access for some populations, but participation is not demonstrated reskilling. Teacher capacity is a local constraint. AI tutors show promising bounded effects, not system-level substitution.
verdict.distribution: Socioeconomic status, migration background, gender, geography, pathway and prior attainment remain material.

questions: What direction are outcomes and pathways moving?
Who gains and who remains excluded?
What competing explanations fit the evidence?

lenses.label: World
lenses.role: Foundational learning and completion, with modelled learning-poverty estimates kept distinct from observations.

lenses.label: Europe / Netherlands
lenses.role: PISA, adult participation, graduate employment and Dutch capacity in their own definitions.

lenses.label: Selected countries
lenses.role: Mechanism comparisons by pathway and institution; not a ranking or a composite.

definitions.label: Assessment boundary
definitions.text: Framework, age, domain and cycle travel together. Scores from different assessments are never spliced.

definitions.label: Adult-learning boundary
definitions.text: Participation is not completion, measured skill gain, occupational transition or earnings.

definitions.label: Pathway boundary
definitions.text: Enrollment is not completion, employment, earnings or job match.

definitions.label: Teacher-capacity boundary
definitions.text: Pupil-teacher ratio is not a vacancy, unqualified-teaching share, workload measure or forecast shortage.

definitions.label: AI evidence boundary
definitions.text: A task effect is not durable learning, teacher substitution, cost reduction or system equity.

foundationalTrajectory.caveat: PISA 2022 mathematics was the major domain. The Dutch sample exceeded the PISA exclusion-rate standard, which may bias results upward. These cycles are not joined to PIRLS, TIMSS, national tests or PIAAC.

measures.label: Advantaged–disadvantaged mathematics gap
measures.subgroupDefinition: top versus bottom national quartile of PISA ESCS

measures.label: Non-immigrant–immigrant mathematics gap after ESCS adjustment
measures.subgroupDefinition: immigrant background means both parents born outside the country of assessment; adjusted for socioeconomic profile

proficiencyDistribution.caveat: Average scores do not replace these distributions. Adjusted gaps are associations, not causal effects of migration background or household resources.

learningPoverty.unit: % of children at late-primary age in low- and middle-income countries
learningPoverty.population: children at late-primary age in low- and middle-income countries
learningPoverty.denominator: children of late-primary age, combining schooling deprivation and reading proficiency
learningPoverty.interpretation: An estimated share unable to read and understand a simple text by age 10.
learningPoverty.caveat: A harmonised composite built from schooling and assessment inputs with modelling for missing and post-disruption outcomes; not a direct universal observation and not comparable to a single PISA percentage.

pathwaySequence.question: Did a learner enter a programme?
Was the credential or final stage completed?
Was a recent graduate employed?
pathwaySequence.measure: employment rate in a defined post-graduation window

pathwaySequence.question: What labour-market return followed?
pathwaySequence.measure: earnings with population and comparison group

pathwaySequence.question: Are acquired capabilities used in the occupation?
pathwaySequence.measure: field or skill match under a stated classification

pathwayEvidence.population: people aged 20–34 who left education 1–3 years earlier and attained ISCED 3–8
pathwayEvidence.denominator: recent graduates meeting the Eurostat definition
pathwayEvidence.interpretation: A high employment rate after upper-secondary through tertiary education.
pathwayEvidence.caveat: Combines medium and tertiary pathways; does not establish completion, earnings, field match, job quality or a causal education effect. Series breaks occurred in 2014 and 2021.

pathwayEvidence.population: recent vocational education and training graduates
pathwayEvidence.denominator: recent VET graduates under the EU indicator definition
pathwayEvidence.interpretation: The EU benchmark concerns exposure during VET, not a demonstrated outcome.
pathwayEvidence.caveat: A target is not an observation; exposure is not completion, employment, earnings or job match.

adultLearning.indicator: Participation in formal or non-formal education and training
adultLearning.referenceWindow: four weeks preceding the EU Labour Force Survey interview
breaks: 2021 break in all country series due to the revised EU Labour Force Survey methodology

distribution.subgroupDenominator: adults aged 25–64 with a low level of educational attainment
distribution.caveat: AES waves and the LFS annual series use different reference windows. Since 2022 the AES collection scope expanded to ages 18–69; the quoted comparison retains ages 25–64.

adultLearning.interpretation: The Netherlands recorded high short-window participation, while participation was lower among adults with low prior attainment in the separate AES.
adultLearning.caveat: Participation records an activity in a window. It does not demonstrate completion, measured skill gain, occupational transition, earnings or successful reskilling.

teacherCapacity.denominator: students weighted by their school principal's response

measures.construct: instruction hindered by lack of teaching staff
instruction hindered by inadequate or poorly qualified teaching staff
instruction hindered by lack of teaching staff

costContext.unit: USD PPP cumulative expenditure per student
costContext.interpretation: Resource level is context, not proof of effective allocation or outcomes.

teacherCapacity.caveat: A principal-reported constraint is not a vacancy count, pupil-teacher ratio, unqualified-teaching share, workload measure or forecast shortage. Student exclusion and response patterns constrain inference.

aiTutorStudies.sample: 194 eligible students in one introductory life-sciences physics course at Harvard; 316 lesson-level post-tests across two lessons
aiTutorStudies.comparator: custom AI tutor at home versus the same content in an in-class active-learning lesson with instructors and peers
aiTutorStudies.duration: two lessons in consecutive weeks; median AI time on task 49 minutes versus 60 assumed instructional minutes in class
aiTutorStudies.outcome: Immediate lesson post-test; linear model effect 0.63 SD, with quantile estimates 0.73–1.3 SD under ceiling effects
aiTutorStudies.uncertainty: Mann–Whitney z = -5.6, p < 10^-8; ceiling effects and lesson-level analysis complicate a single effect estimate
aiTutorStudies.fundingConflicts: No dedicated funding statement was reported on the article page; Harvard units supported production. Authors declared no competing interests.
aiTutorStudies.generalizability: One selective university, one physics course, two lessons, bespoke tutor and immediate tests. No durable retention, cost, equity or teacher-substitution test.

aiTutorStudies.sample: 783 tutors and more than 1,000 K–12 students in a virtual mathematics tutoring programme in one southern U.S. district serving federally funded schools
aiTutorStudies.comparator: human tutors with optional real-time AI suggestions versus the same tutoring platform without Tutor CoPilot
aiTutorStudies.outcome: Access increased unconditional session exit-ticket passing by 4 percentage points; no statistically significant improvement in end-of-year MAP mathematics scores
aiTutorStudies.uncertainty: Exit-ticket ITT estimate 0.040 (SE 0.015), with multiple-testing adjustment; treatment exposure was low and varied by session
aiTutorStudies.fundingConflicts: Working paper produced with FEV Tutor and a partner district; the paper does not provide a standalone funding or competing-interest declaration.
aiTutorStudies.generalizability: Human-AI support for tutors, not an autonomous tutor; short implementation, one provider and district, proximal session outcome.

aiTutorStudies.sample: first-year senior-secondary students in 12 public schools in Edo State, Nigeria
aiTutorStudies.comparator: six-week after-school programme using Microsoft Copilot with teacher facilitation versus usual schooling
aiTutorStudies.outcome: 0.31 SD improvement on an assessment covering English, AI knowledge and digital skills
aiTutorStudies.uncertainty: Study-specific standardized treatment estimate; components and delivery differ from the other trials
aiTutorStudies.fundingConflicts: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper linked to the Edo Basic Education Sector and Skills Transformation Operation; intervention used Microsoft Copilot. Interpret as a working paper, not independent multi-site replication.
aiTutorStudies.generalizability: Short, facilitated after-school programme in one Nigerian state; does not test autonomous replacement, long-run retention or system costs.

aiTutorStudies.sample: about 350 elementary students in two unnamed U.S. districts using an AI literacy platform
aiTutorStudies.comparator: independent AI-platform access versus platform access plus an in-person tutor focused on engagement
aiTutorStudies.duration: intervention windows of 14–31 weeks; active users used the platform for about four to five weeks on average
aiTutorStudies.outcome: Human support raised engagement 71–80%, but usage remained low and reading achievement did not improve
aiTutorStudies.uncertainty: Nearly half of independent-access students never used the platform; platform and districts were unnamed
aiTutorStudies.fundingConflicts: Stanford SCALE / EdWorkingPapers publication; public summary does not disclose the platform or a standalone funding/conflict statement.
aiTutorStudies.generalizability: Evidence about implementation and engagement, not the instructional efficacy of every AI tutor.

poolingDecision.reason: No forest plot or pooled effect: interventions, units of randomization, populations, comparators, durations and outcomes are not commensurable.

primaryGrossEnrollment.label: School enrollment, primary, gross
primaryGrossEnrollment.definition: Total enrollment in primary education, regardless of age, divided by the population of the age group that officially corresponds to primary education.
primaryGrossEnrollment.population: all pupils enrolled in primary education relative to the official primary-school-age population
primaryGrossEnrollment.caveat: A gross access ratio that can exceed 100 because it includes over-age and under-age pupils. Enrollment is not attendance, completion or proficiency.
primaryGrossEnrollment.release: World Development Indicators / UNESCO UIS, source updated 2026-07-13

competingExplanations.label: Cohort composition and coverage
competingExplanations.text: Enrollment, exclusion and migration can change who an assessment represents.

competingExplanations.label: Test mode and framework
competingExplanations.text: Digital transition, domain emphasis and framework changes can alter comparability.

competingExplanations.label: School closures
competingExplanations.text: Closures plausibly contributed, but declines in several systems and domains predated 2020.

competingExplanations.label: Household resources
competingExplanations.text: Language, devices, quiet study space, income and parental time shape opportunity.

competingExplanations.label: Selection into pathways
competingExplanations.text: Learners and employers select into programmes, so raw outcomes do not identify programme effects.

competingExplanations.label: Labour demand
competingExplanations.text: Employment and earnings can move because the economy changes, independently of training quality.

competingExplanations.label: Institutional capacity
competingExplanations.text: Staffing, timetable, curriculum, procurement and implementation determine whether an intervention reaches learners.

reversalIndicators: Sustained recovery across repeated cycles within the same assessment framework, age, domain and mode.
Narrower proficiency and outcome gaps with stable subgroup definitions and denominators.
Credible vocational pathway evidence joining enrollment, completion, employment, earnings and job match without collapsing them.
Repeated adult-learning evidence showing measured skill gains and occupational transitions, especially for adults with low prior attainment.
Reduced vacancies, unqualified teaching and workload pressure under locally valid measures, not only a lower pupil-teacher ratio.
Replicated, independent, long-duration AI-tutor trials showing retention, equity, total costs and safe integration at system scale.

possibilities.label: Hypothesis
possibilities.text: AI may extend feedback and practice when teachers and institutions can integrate it.

possibilities.label: Possibility
possibilities.text: Work-based pathways may improve transitions when employer demand and credential quality align.

possibilities.label: Data gap
possibilities.text: No defensible education/capability composite joins foundational proficiency, adult skill gain, pathway outcomes and teacher capacity.
